## Meaning

This monitor fired because the signal deviated from its own learned baseline by more than the configured number of deviations. It did NOT cross a fixed number, so 'the value looks normal to me' is not a reason to close this.

Query:

```
avg(last_30m):anomalies(avg:system.cpu.user{__SCOPE__} by {cluster,host}, 'agile', 3, direction='above') >= 1
```

**Design note.** Replaces "CPU > 80%". A batch node at 95% on schedule is healthy; an API node at 55% when it normally runs at 20% is not. On its own this is a P3 diagnostic signal; it only becomes a page through event correlation with a service-level symptom.

## Impact

Nothing is broken yet. A boundary will be crossed if nobody acts within the lead time this monitor provides.

Error budget: this condition is associated with `slo-infra-compute-availability`. If the alert is sustained, expect burn-rate alerts on that objective to follow.

## Automation

Workflow `diag-host` (diagnostic only) runs automatically on every alert.

Actions: `fetch_monitor`, `host_process_list`, `disk_usage_breakdown`, `recent_host_events`.

Attached to the alert automatically: top processes, per-mount usage, host event timeline.

## Escalation

1. Owning team: `infrastructure-engineering` (see `platform/policy/teams.yaml` for the channel and ServiceNow assignment group).
2. Escalates to: `sre`.
3. Priority contract: P3 — next business day; this never pages.
